$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}- y=- 2 \cdot y^{2} \cdot e^{\left(x-6\right)}.
$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(1\right)z=2 \cdot e^{\left(x-6\right)}.$$

$$e^{\left(x-6\right)}z=e^{2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=C \cdot e^{- \left(x-6\right)} + e^{\left(x-6\right)}.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\frac{e^{\left(x-6\right)}}{C + e^{2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)}}.$$

Here $C$ is an arbitrary real constant; exclude singularities and restrict to the stated real intervals.

$$
\left(x-6\right)^{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=- 2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{3} \cdot y^{2} + \left(x-6\right) \cdot y.
$$

Work on an interval where $\left(x-6\right)>0$. Choose constants and intervals on which the displayed expressions are real and finite.

{{selection}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, rearrange and divide by the coefficient of the derivative:

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}+- \frac{y}{\left(x-6\right)}=- 2 \cdot \left(x-6\right) \cdot y^{2}. $$

This is a Bernoulli equation with

$$\begin{aligned}p(x)&=- \frac{1}{\left(x-6\right)}\\ q(x)&=- 2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)\\ n&=2.\end{aligned}$$

Divide by $y^{2}$ and set $z=y^{-1}$. The chain rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{1}{y^{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(\frac{1}{\left(x-6\right)}\right)z=2 \cdot \left(x-6\right).$$

An integrating factor is

$$I(x)=e^{\int \frac{1}{\left(x-6\right)}\,\mathrm{d}x}=\left(x-6\right).$$

Multiplying through and using the product rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\left(x-6\right)\,z\right)=2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{2}.$$

Integrating with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$\left(x-6\right)z=\frac{2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{3}}{3}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=\frac{C}{\left(x-6\right)} + \frac{2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{2}}{3}.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\frac{3 \cdot \left(x-6\right)}{3 \cdot C + 2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)^{3}}.$$

Here $C$ is an arbitrary real constant; exclude singularities and restrict to the stated real intervals.
